subject: Renewal: proposal to expand Dedicated pool 8->16 GPUs and amend monthly commit
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@soma.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: proposal to expand Dedicated pool 8->16 GPUs and amend monthly commit

Hi Alex,

Hope you had a good weekend. Our records show the Dedicated capacity agreement for SomaAI (current 8-GPU reserved pool) is up for renewal on 2027-09-15. From our conversations during the pilot, it sounds like you may want to move to a 16-GPU reserved pool and update the monthly commitment to reflect higher throughput.

Attached is a first-pass amendment (renewal_amendment_draft_v1.pdf) that:
- reflects the 8->16 GPU upgrade as an annualized amendment,
- shows two monthly-commit options (conservative/target) with unit pricing, and
- includes suggested SLA targets and a 14-day canary period at elevated capacity.

Before I flesh out pricing further, can you confirm:
1) whether the upgrade would be effective immediately on renewal date (9/15) or if you prefer a phased ramp (we can do 8->12->16 over 30 days),
2) expected monthly token volume (p95/p99) for the next 12 months, and
3) whether procurement/legal need us to route the DocuSign to a specific contact.

Karthik is CC'd to add throughput and latency notes on the feasibility side; Dev is on the thread to confirm billing cadence and any PO requirements.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week if that helps.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: renewal_amendment_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)]
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@soma.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: SomaAI Procurement <procurement@soma.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposal to expand Dedicated pool 8->16 GPUs and amend monthly commit

Irene,

Thanks for the note and the draft. We are interested in moving to 16 GPUs but need two things before we can commit: a clear throughput guarantee (p95 latency target for our typical prompt mix) and a line-item cost comparison that shows estimated monthly spend at 8 vs 16 under steady-state and peak traffic. Procurement will also want the amendment and an updated order form.

A couple of timing notes: procurement is planning a pricing review the week of 8/16 and legal will need at least 7 business days to respond to any contract edits. If possible, can you provide the requested numbers by EOD Friday (8/6)? That will help keep us on track for the 9/15 renewal.

Also, we may ask for a short trial period at 16 GPUs (30 days) to validate our heavier prompt set before we finalize the annual commit. Would Redwood support that?

Regards,
Alex Johnson
VP Engineering, SomaAI
alex.johnson@soma.ai | +1 (617) 555-8484

Alex —

Quick technical notes to help the commercial comparison:
- Baseline: moving from an 8->16 GPU reserved pool doubles peak concurrent slots but actual throughput increases depend on model size, sequence length, and KV cache hit rates. For your Llama-2-Chat-13B workloads we project ~1.8x token/sec at 16 vs 8 under typical prompt distributions.
- Latency: with the right batching settings and a 99th percentile inference SLO target, we can target p95 generation latency of ~220–300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on 16-GPU pool; p99 will depend on burst mixing—can be kept under 800ms with autoscale headroom.
- Canary/trial: recommend a 14–30 day canary with traffic split (10–20%) routed to the 16-GPU pool and close monitoring of tail latency and token cost. We can provide a pre-built throughput projection (attached).

I attached a projection workbook with conservative/expected/peak scenarios and the preferred batching/config knobs for minimal latency impact (throughput_projection.xlsx). Happy to run an on-call test session with your infra team.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
[Attachment: throughput_projection.xlsx (xlsx)]

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Karthik's projections and our commercial templates, we've prepared two formal options in the attached amendment:

Option A (Standard annual commit):
- Effective 2027-09-15, Reserved pool increases to 16 GPUs
- Monthly commit: $X,XXX (reflects 20% volume uplift pricing vs current)
- SLA: 99.5% uptime for dedicated pool, p95 latency objective 300ms for <=128 tokens
- Billing: monthly in arrears; 12-month term

Option B (Phased + trial):
- 30-day elevated trial at 16 GPUs starting on renewal to validate performance
- If trial metrics are met, full annual commit converts at discounted monthly rate $X,XXX
- If not met, option to revert to 8 GPUs for remainder of the term with pro-rated credits for the trial period

I attached an updated amendment that includes line-item pricing and an updated order form. If procurement wants a PO-first flow, Dev can confirm invoicing instructions; otherwise we can send the DocuSign link to your legal contact.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/req/ABC123-soma-renewal
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/SomaAI/renewal-8to16-notes

If the options look good, I can turn this into a redline-ready doc and route to procurement.

Best,
Irene
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
